label: mid-original-phase consonant/digit (k,m,h,t,x,1,...) after an early b/j/g/s/f-type token
explanation: Fires almost entirely during the original (input) phase (91% of mass), from step 3 onward, peaking at positions 3-6 and never at t=0-1. It is driven by the current input: k and m give the highest rates (~20%), then h, t, x, 1, then 2, d, y. Firing is much stronger when tokens from a second group (b, j, g, s, f, and to a lesser degree a, z, i) appeared earlier, especially as the first token; the top examples are sequences like s g j b ... k. It is usually a first occurrence of the input token. Weak, low-magnitude firing also happens on <DEL> and early copy steps when the output is b/j/f/g. It is graded rather than crisp: the predicate gets F1 of about 0.5 on dev, with mass recall of 0.68, and it covers high-activation steps much better than low ones. It does not fire on vowels, c, n, or 0 as inputs, or in the late copy phase.
